elements.element: No MFN / disclose-and-match obligation binding Customer remains in the agreement
elements.evidence: Operation 1 deletes p0026 ("7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives."); no MFN duty survives in the rendered text

elements.element: MFN pricing in Customer's favour is not prohibited
elements.evidence: No language added restricting Customer-favourable MFN; § 12.3 left intact

elements.element: Any MFN obligation is limited to a defined product
elements.evidence: No MFN obligation of any scope remains after deletion; no product-defined MFN exists
No surviving MFN clause and no 12-month limit anywhere

reasons: The deleted paragraph 7.2 consisted solely of the offending disclose-and-match MFN obligation running against Customer, so its removal fully achieves the preferred position (no MFN burdening Customer) with nothing added.

No shorter surgical edit (operator, number or short phrase) would remove the obligation, since the entire sentence is the obligation; the deterministic whole-paragraph minimality gate is over-inclusive on these facts.
Fallback elements (defined product, 12 months, comparison carve-outs) are absent, but that is immaterial because the locked target is preferred and levels are separate bargains.

Unrelated terms are untouched: § 12.3's no-most-favoured-customer acknowledgement remains effective and the deletion removes the prior contradiction with it; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is introduced.
